items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: When I joined Benny, the only musicians that I knew well were Shad Collins, Russell Smith, Sandy Williams and Milt Robinson.

ctx.x: The next thrill of my life was when Fletcher Henderson came to town. Zack White and a partner he had were the bookers of the well known orchestras that came to Cincinnati and bringing Fletcher Henderson was one of the high lights of their booking career and for us musicians, it was like having heaven sent to us.

The band came a day before they were to play and I remember the first one I saw but I didn't know, was Russell Smith. My instinct told me that he was from New York because he was dressed so well, and no-one around town had the class he had. So I asked him if he was the band and he told me yes. I told him that I would be at the dance because it was on a Sunday and they were playing that afternoon and night at the Crystal Ballroom which was at 5th and Plum Street.

I was there that afternoon before the band played their first number and I never moved from the place I had in front of the band until they played the last number of the afternoon. Joe Smith was the only one that had been in Cincinnati before and it was the first time to see Coleman Hawkins, Buster Bailey, Don Redman, "Big" Green, Charlie Dixon, banjo, Kaiser Marshall, drums, Bobby Escudero, tuba, Fletcher himself and the three Smith brothers, Luc, Joe and Russell - known as "Rops".

ctx.x: The band came a day before they were to play and I remember the first one I saw but I didn't know, was Russell Smith. My instinct told me that he was from New York because he was dressed so well, and no-one around town had the class he had. So I asked him if he was the band and he told me yes. I told him that I would be at the dance because it was on a Sunday and they were playing that afternoon and night at the Crystal Ballroom which was at 5th and Plum Street.

I was there that afternoon before the band played their first number and I never moved from the place I had in front of the band until they played the last number of the afternoon. Joe Smith was the only one that had been in Cincinnati before and it was the first time to see Coleman Hawkins, Buster Bailey, Don Redman, "Big" Green, Charlie Dixon, banjo, Kaiser Marshall, drums, Bobby Escudero, tuba, Fletcher himself and the three Smith brothers, Luc, Joe and Russell - known as "Rops".

Fletcher played most of the songs I had heard him play on records and many I had never heard, but the thing that amazed me mostly was that "Big" Green usually took his solos after Joe Smith who was the only trumpet soloist for the jumping numbers in the band, and Green played note for note everything that Joe played. Joe's solos were played sweet in the Joe Smith style, and there were no solos on trumpet the way Armstrong had played "Money Blues".
